title: Telling the story of a trip
goal: Build longer stories about the past with irregular verbs and linking words.
bekal: giving your verdict on an experience
recognizing two past tenses used together

dialogs.title: Diálogo — El viaje a Sevilla
dialogs.intro: A longer story, with the most common irregular past-tense verbs.

lines.speaker: Ana:
lines.text: ¿Qué tal el viaje? ¿Cuándo fuiste a Sevilla?
lines.id: How was the trip? When did you go to Seville?
lines.literal: what such the trip? when you-went to Seville?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: El mes pasado. Estuve allí cinco días.
lines.id: Last month. I was there for five days.
lines.literal: the month past. I-was there five days.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: El primer día visité la catedral. Es enorme.
lines.id: On the first day I visited the cathedral. It's enormous.
lines.literal: the first day I-visited the cathedral. it-is huge.

lines.speaker: Ana:
lines.id: Did you go up the Giralda?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Sí, pero tuve que descansar dos veces. ¡Treinta y cuatro rampas!
lines.id: Yes, but I had to rest twice. Thirty-four ramps!
lines.literal: yes, but I-had that rest two times. thirty and four ramps!

lines.speaker: Ana:
lines.id: And the food? Did you eat well?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Muy bien. Una noche fuimos a un bar de tapas y probé de todo.
lines.id: Really well. One night we went to a tapas bar and I tried a bit of everything.
lines.literal: very well. one night we-went to a bar of tapas and I-tried of everything.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Cuarenta grados. Por eso salíamos solo por la tarde.
lines.id: Forty degrees. That's why we only went out in the evening.
lines.literal: forty degrees. for that we-went-out only through the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Ana:
lines.id: And did you come back wanting to go again?
lines.literal: and you-returned with desire of repeat?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Muchísimas. Fue el mejor viaje de mi vida.
lines.id: Very much. It was the best trip of my life.
lines.literal: very-many(plural). it-was the best trip of my-life.

notes: **Five irregular past verbs cover half of everyday conversation:** *ir / ser* → *fui*, *estar* → *estuve*, *tener* → *tuve*, *hacer* → *hice*, *poder* → *pude*. They all share one feature: **no accent marks at all**, and the stress falls on the second-to-last syllable.
**Hacer has one spelling change:** its *él* form is *hizo*, not *hició* — the c becomes z to keep the same sound. Irregular verbs are like that; their quirks are their calling card.
**Tuve que** = "I had to", the past of *tengo que*. Note its meaning is strong: *tuve que* means you actually did it, not just that you were supposed to.
**Dos veces** = twice. *Vez* is the word for "time" as in "once, twice": *una vez*, *dos veces*, *muchas veces*, *otra vez* (again), *a veces* (sometimes).
**De todo** = "a bit of everything". *Probé de todo* — I tried everything going. Different from plain *todo*, which means all of it, down to the last bit.

**Salíamos** in line 10 is a **different** past tense — the imperfect, for repeated habits during that time. It's covered at A2; here just feel the difference: *fui* happened once, *salíamos* happened again and again.
**Por eso** = "that's why", "so". A very handy connector that makes your story sound organized, not just a list of events.

**El mejor** = the best. *Bueno* has a special form instead of *más bueno*: *mejor* (better / best), and its opposite *peor* — just like English good → better, not "gooder". You met the same kind of pair in Unit 8 with *mayor* and *menor*.

grammars.title: Five must-know past verbs
body: Learn the *yo* and *él* rows first — those two come up most when telling a story.
after: The fifth, *poder*: *pude, pudiste, pudo, pudimos, pudisteis, pudieron*. Notice that the four verbs in the table and *poder* all use **exactly the same** endings — *-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron* — only the stem changes. So what you really need to learn is five stems: *fu-*, *estuv-*, *tuv-*, *hic-*, *pud-*.
Two more with the same pattern that come up often: *decir* → *dije* (I said) and *venir* → *vine* (I came).

blocks.text: The difference between a beginner and someone who sounds fluent is often not vocabulary but connectors. These six words turn a list of events into a story.

head: Español
Meaning
Example
rows: *Llovió, por eso me quedé en casa.*

blocks.title: Speaking practice: tell the story of your weekend
items: Six sentences, no more. The first says when: *El sábado…*
The three middle sentences say what you did, linked with *primero*, *luego*, *más tarde*.
One sentence about someone else: *Mi hermano vino a casa* or *Comimos juntos*.
The last sentence gives a verdict: *Fue un fin de semana tranquilo* or *Fue el mejor fin de semana del mes*.
Do it out loud, and repeat it three times. The third time is almost always much smoother than the first — and that's what you want to take into a real conversation.

blocks.title: Two past tenses, and why you'll hear them mixed
items: Spanish has two past tenses used side by side in one story: the *pretérito* (the one you learned in this unit) for completed events, and the *imperfecto* for background and habits. *Llovía y no salí* — it was raining (background), I didn't go out (event).
In Spain there's one more, the *pretérito perfecto* (*he comido*), for a day that's still going on: *hoy he comido con Marta*. In most of Latin America it's much rarer — people still say *comí*.
So don't panic if what you hear isn't exactly like the tables in this unit. What you have now is enough to be fully understood anywhere, and that's the goal of A1.
If your story stalls, it's fine to use the present with a time marker: *ayer voy a Bogor* isn't correct, but your listener understands and the conversation keeps going. Speak first, polish later.

exercises.prompt: Complete with an irregular past form (*ir*, *estar*, *tener*, *hacer*).
items: El sábado yo ____ a Bogor.
¿Qué ____ tú el fin de semana?
Nosotros ____ en Sevilla cinco días.
Ella ____ que trabajar el domingo.
Ayer ____ mucho calor.
Yesterday I watched a Spanish film.
Last week we went to the beach.
She didn't leave the house last night.
I met the teacher last year.
Last month I was in Seville for five days.
It was the best trip of my life.
¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana?
Llovió todo el día, por eso me quedé en casa.
Tuve que descansar dos veces.
Primero fui a la catedral y luego comí en un bar.
Fue un domingo perfecto.

answers: Ayer vi una película española. — La semana pasada fuimos a la playa. — No salió de casa anoche. — Conocí a la profesora el año pasado. — El mes pasado estuve en Sevilla cinco días. — Fue el mejor viaje de mi vida.
What did you do at the weekend? — It rained all day, so I stayed at home. — I had to rest twice. — First I went to the cathedral and then I ate in a bar. — It was a perfect Sunday.
wave: Close this module by reviewing **Unit 1**: introduce yourself out loud. Sentences you once had to spell out should now come without thinking — the most honest measure of progress there is.
